content.text: The text reviews historical treatment of rectal disorders, including irritable rectum, concretions, proctitis, prolapse, polyps, fistula, hemorrhoids, and rectal hemorrhage, often recommending enemas, cautery, ligation, surgery, or packing. It then discusses rectal alimentation. A lengthy section classifies intestinal parasites—tapeworms, flukes, thorn-headed worms, nematodes, filaria, and trichinae—describing their life cycles, symptoms, treatments, and prevention through hygiene, filtration, and thoroughly cooked food. The final section addresses liver diseases, including biliousness, lithaemia, glycosuria, jaundice, congestion, perihepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatic abscess, emphasizing dietary control, avoidance of alcohol, medicinal therapy, and complications such as ascites, hemorrhage, and suppuration.
